objective: Carry a bounded, versioned observed-attribute map from canonical Observation through reduction into WorldState without creating an unrestricted property channel.
decision_supported: Can parcel, appliance, and managed-slot consumers use observed attributes with strict schema/model parity, per-attribute evidence, deterministic reducer semantics, and explicit aging without weakening the World Model truth boundary?
acceptance: Observation and WorldState expose one strict finite string-to-string attribute map with a maximum of 32 entries, bounded key and value text, printable valid UTF-8, and a canonical serialized-size limit.
The documented vocabulary covers common attributes, parcel identity and condition, appliance door/rack state, and managed-slot state with entity-specific applicability and finite enums.
Unknown or invalid keys and values fail closed at contract or ingestion boundaries; modern attributes cannot bypass per-attribute metadata requirements.

Each modern attribute carries timestamp, finite confidence, evidence references, belief, clock, and source metadata, and metadata ages to stale or lost through an explicit freshness policy and replay boundary.
ActionResult events cannot create or refresh observed attributes.
Complete observations replace the attribute baseline, partial observations merge only named keys after a complete baseline, and provably older per-key updates cannot overwrite newer values.
The canonical WorldState projection and semantic hash include attribute values, schema version, metadata, and evidence needed for deterministic replay integrity.
JSON Schema and Pydantic validation agree on modern metadata, conditional required fields, finite vocabulary, and explicit legacy compatibility.
Parcel payloads have an explicit legacy-observed-attributes-v0 migration path without permitting arbitrary legacy keys.

Focused tests cover bounds, vocabulary, schema/model parity, ingestion materialization, complete/partial updates, legacy migration, action-result isolation, aging, hash changes, and parcel verification quality.
commands: PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 python3 -m pytest tests/unit/test_observed_attributes.py tests/unit/test_world_event_payloads.py tests/unit/test_kernel_schema_compiler.py -q
evidence: Focused contract, ingestion, reducer, verifier, aging, hash, and schema-compiler test output.
Contract, lint, full-test, scenario, context, whitespace, and Task Packet validation output.
Schema/model parity and versioned example validation output.
Changed-path audit showing no firmware, robot-control, simulation, or CI workflow changes.
stop_conditions: The requested behavior requires an ontology service, graph database, arbitrary JSON properties, or a generic property framework.
A public interface change cannot be reviewed together with its Pydantic model and executable tests.
The reducer or verifier would need to infer observed truth from ActionResult or simulator Oracle data.
A write outside the allowed paths is required, especially firmware, robot control, hardware, simulation, or CI workflow code.
Native hardware, physical camera, or hard-real-time evidence is requested but is unavailable in the current Linux environment.
risks_and_fallbacks: Interfaces and contracts require Runtime, World Model, and Integration approval before merge; local tests do not replace those approvals.
Linux validation cannot establish native Windows, physical sensor, actuator, or hard-real-time behavior.
If an existing legacy producer uses a key outside the finite vocabulary, stop and request an explicit contract decision instead of widening validation silently.
